You are writing one SEO/marketing content page for Kodely, an AI website builder (kodely.me). This is real content that will be published live on the site — write it to the same bar as a serious SaaS company's how-to guide, not filler. FACTUAL CONSTRAINTS — read carefully, these override anything in the brief below that conflicts: WHAT KODELY ACTUALLY DOES (real, shipped, verified today): - User describes a site in plain English in a chat interface. - Kodely generates a REAL Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 app — real component files, not a template. - Every project starts from a real foundation with hand-built UI primitives (Button, Card, Section, Nav). - Live preview renders the actual compiled app as it's built. - One-click Publish puts the site live on a real public URL: .kodely.site — free, included. - Further changes: describe them in chat; Kodely edits the real components. - Checkpoints: every successful generation is a restore point; rollback is free. - Code view: see and copy generated source in-app. No zip/full export yet. - Credits: metered from real AI cost. A build that fails to compile is never charged (one automatic repair attempt first). - Free tier: 750 credits on signup, no card required. - Paid top-ups: $9 -> 500 credits, $40 -> 2,500 credits (most popular), $90 -> 6,000 credits. Never expire. - Typical first build: roughly 100-150 credits. - Every publish is scanned for accidentally-leaked secrets before going live. WHAT KODELY DOES NOT DO YET — never claim these: - No backend, database, auth, or payments generation. Output is a real frontend app only. - No custom domains yet — only *.kodely.site. - No code export/download (zip). Only in-app view/copy. - No click-to-edit visual editing — chat-based only. - No "first month of hosting free" — doesn't apply. - No live "Bring it online with Nxeon" integration — not a real page. - Not open-source, not self-hostable. VOICE: Direct, confident, specific, genuinely helpful — this is a TOFU informational guide for someone who's never used an AI builder, so keep jargon low and be concrete. Give a REAL step-by-step walkthrough (signup -> describe -> watch it build -> chat to refine -> publish) and at least one real copy-pasteable example prompt. Include an honest "common mistakes" section (e.g. being too vague in the prompt, not specifying the audience/tone, expecting a working backend when the current product is frontend-only). {"slug":"how-to-build-a-website-with-ai","title":"How to Build a Website with AI","metaTitle":"How to Build a Website with AI (2026 Step-by-Step Guide)","metaDescription":"Build a real website with AI in minutes: describe it in chat, watch Kodely generate live code, refine by chatting, then publish it free to a live public URL.","targetKeyword":"how to build a website with AI","category":"Guides","bodyHtml":"

The old way: templates, page builders, and a lot of manual work

Before AI builders, "building a website" meant one of three paths, and none of them were fast. You could hire a developer and wait weeks for a handful of pages. You could learn HTML, CSS, and a framework yourself, which is a real time investment even for a simple landing page. Or you could pick a drag-and-drop builder or theme and spend hours undoing someone else's design decisions — moving blocks around a template that was never built for your content, your copy, or your brand.

All three paths share the same bottleneck: you're paying for someone else's time, or spending your own, before you see anything real. An AI builder collapses that gap. You describe what you want in plain English, and a working app exists a few seconds later.

How to build a website with AI, step by step

Here's what actually happens when you build a site with Kodely, from a blank tab to a live URL.

1. Create a free account

Go to the signup page and create an account. You don't need a credit card — every new account starts with 750 free credits, which is enough for a full first build (a typical first site runs about 100–150 credits) plus room to make changes afterward.

2. Describe the site you want

You'll land in a chat interface. Instead of picking a template, you type a description of the site you want — what it's for, who it's for, what pages or sections it needs, and any style direction you have in mind. The more concrete you are, the closer the first result lands to what you actually pictured.

3. Watch Kodely generate a real app

Kodely doesn't fill in a template — it generates an actual Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 project, built from a real foundation of hand-built UI primitives (buttons, cards, sections, navigation) rather than a generic component library. You'll see it write and assemble real component files in real time.

4. Preview it live

As soon as the build finishes, the live preview shows you the actual compiled app — not a mockup or a screenshot. What you see is what a visitor would see if you published it right now.

5. Refine it in chat

If something's off, you don't dig through code — you describe the change. "Make the hero section darker," "Add a testimonials section below the pricing cards," "Change the button copy to 'Get Started.'" Kodely edits the real components behind the scenes.

6. Publish it to a live URL

When you're happy with it, click Publish. Your site goes live at a free "yourname.kodely.site" address — no separate hosting step, no configuration.

A copy-paste example prompt to try first

The biggest lever you have on your first result is how specific your prompt is. Instead of "build me a website for my bakery," give Kodely the details it would otherwise have to guess. Try something like this in the chat box:

"Build a one-page website for a small bakery called Maple & Rye. It should have: a hero section with the bakery name, a short tagline, and a button that says 'See Our Menu'; a section showing our four specialties (sourdough, cinnamon rolls, croissants, birthday cakes) as cards with a name and short description each; an 'About Us' section with two paragraphs about our story; and a footer with our address, hours, and a phone number. Use a warm, cozy color palette — cream, brown, and a soft orange accent. Keep the tone friendly and a little playful, not corporate."

Notice what this prompt gives Kodely that a vague one doesn't: the business name, the exact sections and their order, specific content for each section, a color direction, and a tone. That's the difference between a generic result you'll spend ten messages fixing and one you can publish after a couple of tweaks.

What to expect in the preview

The preview panel is a live, compiled render of your actual project — every change you make in chat rebuilds it. A few things worth knowing:

  • What you see is the real app, not a static image. Links, buttons, and layout all behave the way they will once published.
  • Every successful generation creates a checkpoint. If a change in chat takes the design somewhere you don't like, you can roll back to an earlier checkpoint for free — nothing is lost.
  • If a generation fails to compile, Kodely automatically attempts one repair pass before showing you the result, and you're never charged credits for a build that doesn't compile.
  • You can open the code view at any point to see the actual generated source files. There's no export or download yet — code view is for looking and copying snippets, not shipping a zip file.

Refining your site through chat

This is where an AI builder earns its keep over a template. Once the first version exists, you keep talking to it the same way you started it — no drag-and-drop, no visual editor, just plain language:

  • "Swap the hero section for a two-column layout with text on the left."
  • "Make the navigation sticky so it stays visible when scrolling."
  • "Tighten up the spacing between the cards — they feel too far apart."
  • "Change the accent color from orange to teal across the whole site."

Each request edits the real component files, not a copy or an overlay, so changes compound the way they would if you were editing code by hand. If a change doesn't land right, roll back to the last checkpoint and try a more specific version of the same request.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Being too vague in your first prompt. "Make me a website for my business" gives Kodely almost nothing to work with. Name the sections you want, the content that goes in them, and your color or tone preferences up front — you'll spend far fewer follow-up messages fixing structure.
  • Not specifying an audience or tone. "Professional and minimal" and "playful and bold" produce very different sites from the same list of sections. If you don't say which one you want, you'll get whichever the AI guesses — and guessing is where most of your credits go.
  • Trying to fix five things in one message. Bundling "change the colors, rewrite the hero copy, reorder the sections, and add a new page" into one request makes it hard to tell what worked and what didn't. Ask for one clear change at a time, especially early on.
  • Expecting a backend, database, or login system. Today, Kodely generates a real, working frontend — the actual interface a visitor sees and clicks through. It doesn't generate server-side logic, a database, user accounts, or payment processing. If your prompt assumes a contact form that emails you, or a login page that actually authenticates users, the generated UI will look right but won't be wired to anything behind it.
  • Assuming you can export the code today. You can view and copy source from the code view, but there's no zip download or repo export yet. If you need to hand code off elsewhere, plan around copying the pieces you need rather than exporting the whole project.
  • Over-buying credits "just in case." Free accounts start with 750 credits and a first build typically costs 100–150, so most people can iterate for a while before topping up. Check current pack sizes before assuming you need more than you do.

Publishing it live

Publishing isn't a separate deploy process — it's one click. Once you're happy with the preview, click Publish and Kodely puts your site live at a free "yourname.kodely.site" address, included with your account. There's no server to configure and no hosting plan to choose.

Before anything goes live, Kodely automatically scans the build for accidentally-leaked secrets — API keys or credentials that shouldn't be sitting in a public frontend — so a careless prompt or pasted snippet doesn't expose something it shouldn't.

A couple of things worth knowing about publishing today: your site lives at a "kodely.site" subdomain — there's no custom domain support yet — and publishing is free and repeatable, so you can keep refining in chat and republish as many times as you want.

FAQ

Do I need to know how to code?

No. You describe what you want in plain English and Kodely writes the actual React components for you. Code view is there if you're curious or want to copy a snippet, but it's entirely optional.

Is it really free to start?

Yes. New accounts get 750 credits with no card required, which covers a typical first build (roughly 100–150 credits) with room left over for revisions. If you need more later, top-ups run from $9 for 500 credits up to $90 for 6,000, with the $40 / 2,500-credit pack being the most popular — credits never expire. See pricing for the full breakdown.

What happens if a build fails?

Kodely automatically attempts one repair pass on a build that fails to compile. If it still doesn't compile, you aren't charged credits for that attempt.

Can I undo a change I don't like?

Yes. Every successful generation creates a checkpoint, and rolling back to any earlier checkpoint is free.

Can I use my own domain name?

Not yet — published sites live at a free "yourname.kodely.site" address. Custom domain support isn't available today.

Can I add a database, login, or payments?

Not yet. Kodely currently generates a real frontend app — the interface, not backend logic. There's no generated database, authentication, or payment processing at this time.

Can I download or export the code?

You can view and copy the generated source from the in-app code view. A full project export or zip download isn't available yet.

What's next after I publish?

Keep going in the same chat — describe the next change and republish whenever you're ready. You can also browse the blog for more guides, or head back to the homepage to see what else Kodely can do.
